steps.comment: The shape a heavily modded game actually has, which the six-stove run did not: the bill list at vanilla's cap, a lot of pawns scanning, and a wide spread of materials on the floor. Cost in the work-giver prefix is bills x benches x pawns, and the earlier run pinned none of those near their real values.

Five benches. Eight were wanted — bench count is one of the multipliers on every per-scan cost — but the fixture colony has blockers scattered where a longer row lands, and two cells were refused in each of two different layouts. Six is what this fixture reliably supports; a purpose-built flat fixture is what would raise it.

Toxifier generators, not solar, and a conduit run to reach the benches. Every capture from earlier scenarios shows 'Not connected to power' on the inspect pane — a lone generator with no conduits powers nothing, so no bench was ever usable and the ingredient-search path was never really exercised. Toxifier rather than solar because it runs regardless of time of day, so the scenario does not silently depend on the fixture's clock.

Material variety, which is what makes TryFindBestBillIngredients expensive in a modded save and, more to the point for us, what makes ingredient searches fail often enough to exercise the mute path rather than the empty fast path.

Twelve colonists at spacing 2. Twenty at spacing 1 crashed the game natively before it could write a report — pawn generation is expensive and the fixture map is a real colony, so this is the ceiling that survives here rather than the number I wanted.

Tolerant on purpose. The fixture is a real colony with things that move, and successive runs placed 6, then 6, then 5 of the same bench layout — the refused cells differed each time. This scenario exists to measure a hot path at scale, not to pin a bench count, so the check is 'a group of roughly this size formed' and the bill count below is the strict one.

Fifteen bills is BillStack.MaxCount — a group shares vanilla's cap, so this is the largest list this mod can ever be asked to handle, and the ingredient-mute swap used to touch every one of them on every scan of every bench.
Proof the power actually reaches, since 'Not connected to power' is exactly what this scenario was blind to before. Read the inspect line in the capture, not just the pass/fail.
A ceiling well clear of what this run measures, so it fails on a regression rather than on noise.
